einzeiler: Grief expert Dr. Laura Berman discusses navigating loss and her new book.
kurzfassung: Dr. Laura Berman discusses the sudden loss of her son to a fentanyl-laced pill purchased via Snapchat and the release of her new book, Crying Out Loud. She explains the physical and emotional realities of grief, emphasizing the importance of somatic healing and showing up for loved ones. The hosts also share personal experiences with grief and how to better support friends in pain.
stichpunkte: Dr. Laura Berman lost her 16-year-old son Sammy to fentanyl poisoning after he bought drugs through Snapchat.
Fentanyl is present in 65% of street drugs and is extremely potent and addictive.
Grief is a form of trauma that affects the body physically, requiring somatic release rather than just cognitive coping.
Dr. Berman compares trying to avoid grief to cows running away from a storm, whereas facing it directly is like bison charging through it.
Grief does not get smaller over time; instead, individuals must expand their capacity to hold it.
Supporters should take action rather than asking grieving individuals what they need, as grievers often do not know.
Couples frequently grieve differently, and it is vital to respect each other's coping mechanisms.
Allowing oneself to feel deep pain increases the capacity to experience joy.

kapitel.titel: Welcoming Dr. Laura Berman and Sammy's Story
The Healing Journey and Somatic Work
How Friends and Partners Can Support Grievers
Psilocybin and Alternative Tools for Trauma

clips.hook: Fentanyl dangers and social media drug dealers
clips.text: The guest explains the extreme lethality and addictiveness of fentanyl, noting that street drugs frequently contain it and predators sell substances to minors via Snapchat.

clips.hook: Do not be afraid to say the name of a lost loved one
clips.text: Grieving parents want people to speak their deceased child's name and acknowledge special dates rather than avoiding the topic out of fear.

clips.hook: The bison metaphor for facing grief head-on
clips.text: While cows run away from storms and prolong their suffering, bison charge directly into the storm so it passes over them more quickly.

clips.hook: The connection between allowing pain and feeling joy
clips.text: Emotions travel through the same channel, meaning that suppressing sadness also limits a person's ability to experience deep joy.

clips.hook: Stop asking grieving friends what they need
clips.text: Grieving individuals are often overwhelmed and unable to process requests, so supporters should simply take action and provide help directly.

beschreibung:
Grief doesn’t follow a timeline, and it doesn’t simply get smaller. After losing her 16-year-old son Sammy, therapist Dr. Laura Berman had to learn how to survive the unimaginable. She joins Bill and Giuliana to share what grief really does to the mind and body, why the only way out is through, and how we can better show up for the people we love.
Bill also opens up about losing his father and the choice he made to keep living fully in his honor. Dr. Berman’s new book, Crying Out Loud: A Path Through Grief into a Life Reimagined, is available now for pre-order.
